claims: Final pay adds outstanding wages, unused annual leave, notice in lieu, long service leave and any redundancy pay, taxed at your marginal rate
whys: The code (lines 77-87) applies the overall effective rate (income tax less LITO plus Medicare, divided by salary) to the non-redundancy parts and leaves redundancy pay untaxed, so the page does not use the marginal rate. Under ATO rules, payment in lieu of notice and genuine redundancy above the tax-free limit are employment termination payments (ETP), and some unused leave gets concessional rates, so 'everything at your marginal rate' is also wrong as a rule. The disclaimer at line 220 already says 'effective rate'.
constants: final-pay-calculator.tsx tax logic (lines 77-87); ETP cap and genuine redundancy tax-free limit constants if they exist in lib/constants

claims: HECS-HELP repayments for employees with a study debt above {HECS_HELP.minimumThreshold}
whys: The HELP threshold applies to repayment income, not to the size of the study debt. Line 333 states the rule correctly.

claims: The Medicare levy of 2% applies to all taxable income above the low-income threshold
whys: Read literally, this says the levy is charged only on income above the threshold. In fact there is a shade-in range above the low-income threshold, then 2% of the whole taxable income.
constants: MEDICARE_LEVY in lib/constants (lowIncomeThreshold, shade-in upper threshold)

claims: Your salary does not rise that year; it is spread over one more pay
whys: This is employer-dependent. Many employers pay 27 full fortnightly amounts (annual / 26). That is the case the ATO's optional extra withholding covers. The sentence states one practice as the rule.

claims: the {TAX_BRACKETS.length} income tax brackets for FY2026-27
whys: The year is typed in by hand while every other figure uses SITE_CONFIG.financialYear, so it will go stale at the next financial-year rollover. The 1 July 2027 rate change and the $250 Working Australians Tax Offset at line 168 are also typed in by hand.
constants: SITE_CONFIG.financialYear; WATO amount and future 15%->14% rate in lib/constants

claims: Overtime is 'paid at penalty rates of 1.5x (time and a half) or 2.0x (double time)'
whys: Awards and Fair Work treat overtime rates and penalty rates as separate things, and overtime multipliers depend on the award (often 1.5x for the first 2 or 3 hours, then 2x). The text states them as a universal rule. I could not change 'penalty rates' to 'overtime rates' because a test or script matches the text 'penalty rates'.
constants: EMPLOYMENT / award overtime data; 'penalty rates' test literal

claims: Leave loading of 17.5% is paid 'under many awards and enterprise agreements'
whys: Population claim with no count and no source cited on the page (brief lesson: population claims go to factQuestions).

claims: Medicare levy written as a literal '2%' at lines 79, 193 and 228, plus 'applies to most Australian residents' at line 79
whys: The figure is correct today (MEDICARE_LEVY.rate = 0.02), but it is typed into the copy while the lead paragraph uses MEDICARE_PCT, so it will not change if the constant does. 'Most Australian residents' is a population claim with no source.
